text: You finally order that small, perfect gadget online. A few days later, it arrives. But wait… why is it in *this*?
You tear open a ridiculously oversized box, revealing your tiny item swimming in a sea of packaging. It feels like such a waste.
Your first thought might be, "they just ran out of small boxes," or "someone was lazy." But the truth is much deeper than a simple mistake.
Online retailers use a limited set of standardized box sizes. This allows for automated packing, efficient storage, and faster shipping through complex conveyor systems.
Custom-sizing every single package would require endless box types, specialized machinery, and vastly more human labor, slowing everything down and skyrocketing costs.
The cost of a little extra cardboard and air in your delivery is far less than the cost of a perfectly fitted box. Now you see the invisible system behind the "waste."
